milestones.title: M0 — Public foundation
milestones.description: Clean public baseline, FOSS terms, CI, issue-backed kanban, and a pinned rules/conformance process.

milestones.title: M1 — Commander-ready multiplayer kernel
milestones.description: Deterministic 2–4-seat turn order, priority, elimination, private projections and versioned replay. Still not a claim of Commander card support.

milestones.title: M2 — Playable Commander vertical slice
milestones.description: 40-life Commander profile, command zone/tax/damage, required mechanics and an explicitly certified starter-deck corpus.

milestones.title: M3 — Native table and learning
milestones.description: A usable four-seat graphical table, complete practice controls, exact two/four-deck import, accessible priority/stack teaching and study branches.

milestones.title: M4 — Stronger play, measured
milestones.description: Budgeted information-safe search, optional local model, paired evaluation and an honestly scoped comparison suite.

milestones.title: v1.0 — Release candidate
milestones.description: Installable, reproducible, reviewed FOSS release with verified curated Commander games and no unsupported universal-coverage claims.

issues.title: Publish the clean, history-preserving FOSS baseline
acceptance: Publish the existing reachable commit history without squashing or force-pushing.
Provide MIT OR Apache-2.0 license texts matching Cargo metadata.
Audit reachable blobs for credentials; document test-only false positives without publishing tokens.
Read back the remote branch SHA and confirm a clean local worktree.

issues.title: Run locked Rust quality gates on Linux, Windows and macOS
acceptance: GitHub Actions runs format, all-target tests and Clippy with warnings denied on all three runners.
Pin third-party actions to immutable commit SHAs and use read-only workflow permissions.
Verify the exact published revision and record actual CI conclusions, not launch acknowledgements.

issues.title: Set contribution, security and third-party asset boundaries
acceptance: Document RED/GREEN development, review, branch ownership and evidence requirements.
Publish a safe vulnerability-reporting route and prohibit credentials/weights/cache in commits.
Keep original engine source licensing separate from third-party card text, art, rules and model licenses.
Make unsupported features and the current practice-only scope prominent.

issues.title: Publish the live issue-backed v1 kanban
acceptance: Create milestone issues with dependencies and executable acceptance criteria.
Display Backlog, Ready, In progress, Review, Blocked and Done from GitHub issue state/labels.
Handle search, milestone filtering, API failures and a visibly dated offline snapshot.
Document status transitions; never require a token in the browser.

issues.title: Pin rules provenance and build a conformance case format
acceptance: Record the official Comprehensive Rules document revision, source URL and SHA-256 without guessing the latest revision.
Define fixtures with initial state, actions, expected decisions/events and applicable rule references.
Seed timing, state-based action, cleanup and multi-blocker damage cases; distinguish intentional simplifications.
Publish a procedure to review new rules revisions without silently changing old replays.

issues.title: Generalize state and turn order to 2–4 live seats
acceptance: Replace implicit two-player assumptions with validated ordered seats while preserving current two-seat behavior.
Cover active-player advancement, turn wraparound and eliminated-seat skipping for 2, 3 and 4 seats.
Reject duplicate/invalid seat configurations without panics or silent repair.
All existing tests pass; new behavior has retained RED/GREEN evidence.

issues.title: Implement multiplayer priority and elimination scheduling
acceptance: Rotate priority through all eligible live seats in turn order.
Resolve exactly one stack object only after every eligible player passes in succession; reset passes on a response.
Model APNAP ordering as a pending player choice where required, never an AI guess.
Test active/nonactive player elimination, priority owner elimination and last-player wins.

issues.title: Protect hidden information for every multiplayer viewer
acceptance: Project all public opponents without exposing private hands, library order or unentitled pending choices.
Test every seat with deliberately unequal life totals, hands and library sizes.
Ensure legal choices and AI observations belong to the acting seat, not the human or a hard-coded opponent.
Keep public reveal knowledge explicit and scoped; no omniscient evaluator leaks into normal play.

issues.title: Version multiplayer save and replay without silent corruption
acceptance: Store format, ordered seats, exact deck snapshots and replay schema version.
Choose explicit migration or explicit rejection for old saves; never silently reinterpret seat count.
Prove deterministic digests for fresh three/four-seat games and save/load/pending-choice round trips.
Reject malformed replay input with a useful error rather than panic.

issues.title: Deliver a four-seat headless regression harness
acceptance: Run terminal 2/3/4-seat practice games across fresh paired seeds with bounded timeout handling.
Verify every emitted replay digest and classify terminal, capped and failed games separately.
Adapt policy/CLI/UI call sites to the new interfaces without falsely exposing an unsupported Commander toggle.
Record raw machine-readable results and keep existing native two-seat practice playable.

issues.title: Validate Commander deck profiles and color identity
acceptance: Represent commanders separately and validate the supported 100-card singleton profile with basic-land exceptions.
Check color identity and commander eligibility from authoritative metadata, including required face rules.
Handle supported partner/background variants explicitly or refuse them with an exact unsupported reason.
Report format legality separately from engine/card support; no silent card/deck substitution.

issues.title: Implement command zone, commander tax and zone-change choices
acceptance: Start supported commanders in the command zone and track each commander independently.
Apply commander tax from command-zone casts only, including repeated casts and multiple commanders where supported.
Model the applicable command-zone replacement/state-based choices with correct timing and object identity.
Cover refusal, acceptance, resolution failure and replay/save round trips.

issues.title: Track commander combat damage, 40 life and player loss
acceptance: Use 40 starting life only for the Commander profile; retain named practice profiles.
Track combat damage by commander identity and recipient; distinguish it from noncombat damage.
Test the 21-damage loss condition, control changes, prevention and multiple commanders independently.
Remove eliminated-player objects and choices according to the pinned rules, including stack corner cases.

issues.title: Add typed activated and triggered ability scheduling
acceptance: Represent costs, targets, modes and ability sources independently of UI and AI.
Support required starter-corpus activated/triggered abilities through legal player decisions.
Test simultaneous triggers/APNAP, mandatory versus optional triggers, missed targets and last-known information.
Do not use free-form model output as rules code or automatic state-based actions.

issues.title: Add replacement, prevention and layered continuous effects
acceptance: Define an effect pipeline with explicit dependency/timestamp handling for supported layer interactions.
Offer affected-player choices when multiple applicable replacements require a choice.
Cover prevention, destruction versus zero toughness, duration expiry and last-known information.
Keep unimplemented interaction families explicitly unsupported in certification.

issues.title: Implement counters, tokens, keywords and library operations
acceptance: Use typed object/player counters, including +1/+1, -1/-1 and required starter-corpus counters.
Implement token creation/cessation and the keyword set actually required by certified decks.
Provide untap, draw, mill, scry, surveil, reveal, shuffle and targeted/library choices with correct visibility.
Test interaction with replacements, triggers, state-based actions, replay and controller changes.

issues.title: Certify the v1 Commander starter corpus end to end
acceptance: Publish at least eight explicitly supported 100-card Commander lists spanning different play styles.
Every included card and required interaction has an implementation and conformance coverage.
Play four-seat games using exact deck snapshots, never bundled replacements.
Document per-card/interaction exclusions; arbitrary Archidekt compatibility remains an explicit non-goal until proven.

issues.title: Build a readable native four-seat Commander table
acceptance: Display all four battlefields, commanders, life, counters, public zones and player status.
Expose own hand, actionable pending choices and stack/priority ownership without hidden information leaks.
Keep table and primary controls usable at 1280x720 and on a large monitor; include zoom/inspect and keyboard navigation.
Verify actual clicks and viewport behavior on the packaged binary, not only a screenshot.

issues.title: Teach stack, priority and rules from the actual trace
acceptance: Explain why actions are legal/illegal using the pinned rule and current decision state.
Show consecutive passes, response windows, APNAP choices and what resolves next.
Separate verified rule explanations from strategic suggestions and disclosed simplifications.
Provide guided walkthrough fixtures and tests for intricate interactions; do not invent model explanations.

issues.title: Deliver tabletop-grade practice and zone controls
acceptance: Provide searchable/inspectable zones, explicit draw/untap/mill/scry/surveil/reveal controls and counter editors.
Separate legal-match actions from labelled sandbox overrides that taint the competitive record.
Keep undo/study behavior honest about hidden information and deterministic random state.
Use confirmation and meaningful error states for destructive reset/import/load actions.

issues.title: Make Archidekt import a complete Commander start flow
acceptance: Accept canonical public Archidekt URLs for the human and each AI seat with text/file fallbacks.
Preserve commanders, categories, quantities, side exclusions and exact validated lists.
Show legality, unsupported mechanics and support counts before enabling match start; retain URL guard/redirect/size limits.
Keep HTTP/disk work off the frame thread and discard stale imports after session changes.

issues.title: Harden responsiveness, accessibility and input ergonomics
acceptance: Provide keyboard/focus operation, scalable text, high contrast and non-color-only status indicators.
On named reference hardware, target p95 frame time below 33 ms and input response below 100 ms during delayed AI/network work.
Cover small window, high-DPI, long deck reports, large boards and reduced-motion behavior.
Record reproducible measurements and manual input evidence; targets are not claimed results until measured.

issues.title: Add review, study branches and multiplayer persistence
acceptance: Save/load a live four-seat session with pending stack/choice state intact.
Branch from a replay and compare accepted actions without leaking future/private information by default.
Offer an explicit postgame omniscient review mode separate from normal policy inputs.
Keep stale-worker generation guards valid across every load, branch, import and reset.

issues.title: Build budgeted information-set search behind the legal-action API
acceptance: Keep legality and state transitions in the deterministic Rust engine; policies select only offered actions.
Use reproducible determinizations/information-set search without accessing real opponent hands or future library order.
Provide cancellation, decision budgets, progressive analysis and a deterministic legal fallback.
Evaluate improvements against the frozen heuristic rather than equating larger search with stronger play.

issues.title: Integrate the optional local decision model honestly
acceptance: Use viewer-masked observations and revision/decision/seat/session-generation validation.
Reject malformed, stale, truncated or illegal outputs and expose a deterministic fallback reason.
Keep the model optional, offline-capable and separately licensed; do not bundle weights without authorization.
Report preference concentration separately from calibrated outcome estimates or search evaluations.

issues.title: Publish paired-seed AI strength and latency evidence
acceptance: Use at least 1000 paired games/rotations on the certified corpus with budgets and hardware pinned.
Report seat/deck bias, terminal versus capped outcomes, wall-clock latency and confidence intervals.
Gate a stronger-than-baseline claim on a confidence interval above parity for the declared matchup set.
Store raw reports, versioned configs and verified replay digests; no cherry-picked probes.

issues.title: Benchmark the product against existing engines and tabletop apps
acceptance: Select pinned versions of Forge, XMage and relevant graphical tabletop alternatives from primary sources.
Measure overlapping rules scenarios, certified-deck support, import friction, setup time, accessibility and responsiveness.
Publish gaps and losing comparisons as well as wins; label unavailable or unexecuted results.
Define specific superiority claims per measured dimension; never advertise better in every way without evidence.

issues.title: Add chess-style move review without false certainty
acceptance: Rank alternatives using reproducible search under a stated information boundary and compute budget.
Show candidate lines, uncertainty and practical reasons for alternatives from legal traces.
Keep engine rule explanations separate from policy preferences; avoid fake win probabilities and forced blunder labels.
Validate teaching quality on a reviewed interaction/strategy corpus.

issues.title: Ship reproducible desktop packages and release artifacts
acceptance: Build versioned Windows, Linux and macOS artifacts in CI using a locked dependency graph.
Include licenses, support manifest, bundled certified decks, changelog and checksums.
Smoke-test downloaded packages in clean working directories without local model services.
Publish a candidate before stable v1; document platform signing/notarization status honestly.

issues.title: Pass clean-machine platform and accessibility acceptance
acceptance: Exercise import → start → priority/stack choice → save → load → finish on each claimed platform.
Verify actual native input and supported viewport/high-DPI behavior.
Test offline use, slow/failed imports, missing model, failed saves and stale background results.
Keep defects open until the exact packaged revision passes the failing journey.

issues.title: Audit dependencies, untrusted inputs and third-party distribution
acceptance: Run dependency/license and credential audits and triage findings with evidence.
Fuzz or systematically mutate import/replay/save inputs, URL handling and action validation.
Review distributed card/rules/art/model content and notices separately from original engine licenses.
No unresolved high-severity security issues, private data leaks or unlicensed bundled assets at release.

issues.title: Run the Commander conformance and determinism release soak
acceptance: Run at least 1000 certified four-seat games with declared seed/deck rotation coverage.
Require zero unexplained panics, accepted illegal actions, hidden-information leaks or replay mismatches.
Retain capped runs and failures as failures or explicit exclusions, never successful completed games.
Review conformance results against the pinned rules and publish every remaining supported-scope limitation.

issues.title: Approve v1 only after every release gate is evidenced
acceptance: Require closed release blockers and reviewed conformance, UI, AI, security and packaging reports.
Publish exact support scope, known limitations, migration notes, reproducible benchmarks and source.
Verify downloadable artifacts/checksums and the final tag/commit before announcing v1.
Make no universal card-coverage or best-engine claim; superiority claims must link to reproducible comparisons.
